issues.display_title: Issue #60: MultiView: Stack 360 Images Vertically (One on top of the other), Not Side by Side
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback

Problem

In MultiView / compare mode, 360 (equirectangular/panorama) images are arranged side by side (horizontally). Because 360 images are wide (2:1), a side-by-side layout makes each one small and hard to inspect.

Request

For 360 images, stack the views vertically — one on top of the other — instead of side by side. This gives each wide panorama more horizontal room and matches how 360 content is best compared.

Scope

  • In MultiView, change the layout so 360 images stack vertically (rows) rather than horizontally (columns).
  • Applies specifically to 360/panorama images (confirm behavior for non-360/flat images — likely keep as-is).
  • Preserve existing MultiView features (up to 8 views, sync, per-tile controls).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When comparing 360 images in MultiView, tiles are stacked vertically (one above the other), not side by side.
  2. Each 360 image gets full available width, improving visibility.
  3. MultiView still supports its existing max count and controls.

issues.display_title: Issue #77: Modernize the app's internal data-handling layer for reliability
issues.main_description_html:
Second step in the ongoing front-end cleanup effort (builds on the code quality setup from the previous step).

The app keeps track of things like which files are loaded, what's currently being edited, and user settings using a central internal data store. This step upgrades how that store is accessed throughout the app, adding safety checks that catch a whole class of bugs automatically before they ever reach users.

What changed for users: Nothing — this is entirely behind-the-scenes work. No visual or functional changes.

Why it matters: Reduces the risk of subtle bugs in file handling, editing tools, and settings, and makes the codebase easier and safer to build new features on top of.

Part of the larger front-end refactor initiative. Builds on the code quality setup (previous issue). See PR #75.

issues.display_title: Issue #72: Fix Issue Manual Leveling Output is Severely Distorted and Does Not Match UI Preview
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A critical issue has been reported in the Manual Leveling tool (GoThru Photo Studio v1.1.4). When a user adjusts the Roll, Pitch, and Yaw sliders, the horizon appears correctly leveled within the tool's live preview canvas. However, after applying the changes, the resulting equirectangular output image is severely distorted with an exaggerated, curved horizon.

User Notes:

  • The live preview inside the Manual Leveling tool correctly reflects the intended adjustments.
  • The final processed image does not match the preview at all.
  • Auto-leveling is functioning correctly, but users cannot rely on it for every image, making manual leveling a blocker for their workflow.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "the manual leveling does not work properly. this is what I set … and this is what I get. auto leveling seems to be OK but auto level does not work for all of them." (Screenshots: correct in-tool preview vs. distorted final output.)

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open an uneven 360 image in the application.
  2. Navigate to the Manual Leveling tool.
  3. Adjust the Roll, Pitch, and Yaw sliders to straighten the horizon in the preview (e.g., Yaw: -110.4).
  4. Click Apply to process the image.
  5. Open the resulting image in the main Preview viewer.
  6. Observe that the horizon is highly distorted/curved rather than straight.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The mathematical transformation applied to the final image perfectly matches the WebGL preview shown in the UI.
  2. Users can manually adjust Roll, Pitch, and Yaw, and the resulting saved image maintains a straight, correct horizon.

issues.display_title: Issue #76: Set up code quality standards for the app's front-end codebase

issues.display_title: Issue #66: Handle Issue "Edit" Button Routes to Last Active Tool Instead of Main Tools Edit Dashboard
issues.main_description_html:
A UX/routing issue has been reported in GoThru Photo Studio (v1.1.4). When a user clicks the "Edit" button in the top navigation bar, the application remembers their previous state and routes them directly back into the last specific tool they had open (e.g., Image Minifier or AI Nadir Patching).

The expected behavior is that the "Edit" button should act as a hard reset for that section. Clicking it should always land the user on the main Tools Dashboard (the grid view displaying all available editing tools), regardless of what tool they were using previously.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "There is a problem with the Edit button, it takes me the last tool I had open. It should always take me to see all the Tools." Annotated screenshot shows the Edit button should land on the Tools grid, not inside a tool.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Clicking the "Edit" button from anywhere in the app (File Manager, Preview, etc.) always opens the main Tools grid showing all available tools.
  2. Clicking the "Edit" button while actively inside a specific editing tool safely unmounts that tool and returns the user to the main Tools grid.
  3. The routing change does not cause data loss if a user accidentally navigates away while processing an image (ensure standard unmount warnings still apply if a job is running).

🧪 Testing Scenario (for QA)

Feature: "Edit" button in the top navigation bar
Goal: Verify the Edit button always resets to the main Tools grid, never re-opening the last tool.

Pre-conditions

  • App running (v1.1.4+), a folder with images opened.

Test 1 — Edit reopens Tools grid (not last tool)

  1. Click Edit → open a specific tool (e.g. Image Minifier).
  2. Navigate away: click File Manager (or Preview).
  3. Click Edit again.
  • ✅ Expected: Lands on the main Tools grid (all tools visible).
  • ❌ Fail: Reopens Image Minifier (or whatever tool was last used).

Test 2 — Edit while inside a tool

  1. Open Edit → AI Nadir Patching (or any tool).
  2. While inside that tool, click Edit in the top nav again.
  • ✅ Expected: The tool unmounts cleanly and the main Tools grid is shown; no leftover tool UI/state.

Test 3 — From every entry point

  1. From File Manager, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  2. From Preview, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  3. After using a tool then returning, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  • ✅ Expected: Every path lands on the Tools grid.

Test 4 — No data loss while a job is running

  1. Open a tool and start processing an image (job running).
  2. Click Edit in the top nav to navigate away.
  • ✅ Expected: Standard unmount/leave warning appears (per existing behavior); confirming does not corrupt or silently drop the running job; cancelling keeps the user in the tool.

Regression checks

  • Other nav buttons (Preview, File Manager, Upload) still work.
  • Selecting a tool from the grid still opens it normally.
  • Repeating Edit → tool → Edit multiple times stays consistent (no sticky state).

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

issues.display_title: Issue #78: Fix broken AI image generation and make AI model settings remotely updatable
issues.main_description_html:
AI-powered features (Nadir Patching, Room Staging, and Virtual Staging) were silently failing for some users because the app was pointing to an outdated AI model name that no longer works the way the code expected.

This fix corrects the immediate issue and, more importantly, makes the AI model names configurable remotely. This means if the AI provider renames or updates their models again in the future, the team can fix it instantly without having to release a new version of the app.

What changed for users: AI Nadir Patching, Room Staging, and Virtual Staging should now generate images reliably instead of failing silently.

Why it matters: Prevents a recurring class of "broken until we ship an update" issues for AI features, and restores functionality that was quietly broken for some users.

See PR #74.

issues.display_title: Issue #67: Fix Issue "Preview" Button Loads Incorrect Folder Context from Inside Editing Tools
issues.main_description_html:
A critical context loss bug has been reported. When a user is working inside an editing tool (such as "Auto Level") within a specific folder, and they click the "Preview" button in the top navigation bar, the application routes them to the Preview screen but fails to maintain the current folder's context.

Instead of previewing the images from the folder they were just working in, the system loads a Preview state from an entirely different, previously accessed folder.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "There is a bug, let's say I am in a tool like Auto Level, and I click Preview, it takes me back to Preview from another folder, not the current folder."

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When a user is inside an editing tool (e.g., Auto Level) for Folder A, clicking "Preview" successfully opens the Preview screen populated with the images from Folder A.
  2. The application never loads images from Folder B (a previous session) when transitioning to Preview from Folder A.

🧪 Testing Scenario (for QA)

Feature: "Preview" button navigation from inside an editing tool
Goal: Verify Preview always shows the CURRENT folder's images, never a previously opened folder.

Pre-conditions

  • App running (v1.1.4+); at least two different folders with images available (call them Folder A and Folder B).

Test 1 — Core repro (current folder context preserved)

  1. Open Folder B, go to Preview at least once (to seed a previous Preview state), then leave.
  2. Open Folder A.
  3. Enter an editing tool for Folder A, e.g. Edit → Auto Level.
  4. While inside Auto Level, click Preview in the top nav.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview opens populated with Folder A images (the folder currently being worked on).
  • ❌ Fail: Preview shows Folder B images (stale/previous-session context).

Test 2 — Multiple tools

  • Repeat Test 1 using other tools (e.g. Image Minifier, AI Nadir Patching) to confirm the fix is not tool-specific.

Test 3 — Multiple folder switches

  1. Open Folder A → Preview → back.
  2. Open Folder B → enter a tool → click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder B (the latest/current folder), not Folder A.

Test 4 — Fresh session / single folder

  1. Open only Folder A (no prior Preview history), enter a tool, click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder A correctly (no empty/incorrect state).

Regression checks

  • Preview opened directly from File Manager still shows the correct current folder.
  • Image count and file details panel in Preview match Folder A's contents.
  • Navigating tool → Preview → back to tool keeps Folder A context intact.

issues.display_title: Issue #84: Implement Control Point for Stitch 360
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-17.at.6.26.34.PM.1.mp4

The "Control Point" feature in Stitch 360 (lets a user mark the same spot on two photos so the panorama lines up more accurately) is now actually wired into the photo-stitching process — before this, it was just a UI, the points a user drew were never used.

Done:

  • User can create points from scratch (no need for an automatic alignment pass first)
  • Those points are now actually used when the photos are merged into a panorama
  • Covered by automated tests (18 tests) + 1 real test using actual photos, all passing
  • The photo-stitching engine (pt-stitch) was also updated to the latest version

Still needed:

  • Manual testing in the running app — open the app, mark real points on real photos, run a stitch, check the result looks right. This has not been tried at all yet.
  • The Mac build of the stitching engine hasn't been updated yet (Windows only so far)

PR: #83 (not merged yet, waiting on the manual test above)
